description:
The graceful-shutdown drain assertions observe what they assert, so the whole-workspace suite stops failing on a correct server.

## Background

`test_jit_server_shutdown_force_closes_a_stalled_connection_and_exits_zero` is `#[ignore]`d. It failed the `cargo-ci` gate on three separate commits of a correct server, and passes ten times out of ten when run alone. Two independent causes were established while wave 0 of `e204e63d` was gating.

The first is a deadline race. The test sends `SIGTERM`, then waits out three other connections, each entitled to its own `STREAM_EOF_BUDGET`, before asserting that the stalled connection is still open partway through the drain. Those waits together may exceed `GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT`, and once they do a correct server has already force-closed the survivor, so the assertion fails on conforming behaviour. In isolation the waits return in milliseconds and the probe lands mid-drain, which is why the failure never reproduces alone. A guard now takes the probe only while the deadline is intact; that half is fixed and is not what remains.

The second is an acceptance race, and it is what the ignore is for. `open_stalled_connection` sends a partial request and returns as soon as the bytes are written, with nothing establishing that the server has accepted and registered the connection. When `SIGTERM` arrives before the accept loop takes it, the socket is not a live connection the drain is obliged to protect, and it dies with the listener. The signature is a run that completes in about a second where a passing run takes the full drain.

The design question this issue must answer is how a test establishes that the server has registered a connection whose request is deliberately incomplete. No response is readable by construction, the server exposes no live-connection count to a client, and sampling the log is itself timing-dependent. A round trip on a second connection proves the accept loop ran but not that this socket was the one taken.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The test establishes that the server has registered the stalled connection before the shutdown signal is sent, by an observation that cannot pass while the connection is still unaccepted.
- [hard] REQ-02: The test is no longer `#[ignore]`d and runs in the default `cargo test --workspace` run.
- [hard] REQ-03: The suite passes repeatedly under the contention a whole-workspace run produces, evidenced by consecutive whole-workspace runs rather than by running the test alone.
- [hard] REQ-04: The properties the test asserted before this change are all still asserted: the event streams reach EOF under cancellation, an idle keep-alive connection is retired by the graceful shutdown, the connection that cannot finish keeps the drain it is entitled to, and the process exits zero within its budget.
- [hard] REQ-05: No assertion is weakened to a form that would pass against a server that force-closes a live connection before `GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT`.

## Notes

The deadline-race guard already landed as `fix(jit:e204e63d)` and is not to be reverted; it is correct on its own terms and addresses a genuinely separate cause. This issue owns the acceptance race and the removal of the `#[ignore]`.

Ignoring the test removes graceful-shutdown coverage from the authoritative `cargo-ci` gate, so `e204e63d` depends on this issue: that container may not close while the coverage its own gating disabled is still missing.
title: Observe the drain assertions the graceful-shutdown test makes
